ticks.note: Tick 1: `reply` gets the literal `"hi"`. The self-loop is delayed, so nothing is compared yet.

`reply == "hi"` is true, but `name == "hi"` is false although `name` is "hi" too. In the C code strings are pointers: `reply` points at the same literal `"hi"`, while the input's text lives somewhere else.
`nameIsHi` is false whatever `name` holds: an input string never compares equal to a literal.
